```{r libraries, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
if (!require("pacman")) install.packages("pacman")
p_load(tidyverse, DBI, RPostgres)
```

```{r db_connection, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
con <- dbConnect(
  RPostgres::Postgres(),
  dbname = 'pr_labor_proj',
  host = "localhost",
  port = 5432,
  user = Sys.getenv("DB_USER"),
  password = Sys.getenv("DB_PASSWORD")
)

acs_01_24 <- tbl(con, "data_acs")
```

```{r Age adjusted LFPR, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# 2. Server-Side Data Prep and Aggregation
# This entire block runs on your PostgreSQL server, not in R memory
server_aggregated_data <- acs_01_24 %>%
  # Filter for working-age population and valid labor force codes
  filter(AGE >= 16, LABFORCE %in% c(1, 2), YEAR >= 2001, YEAR <= 2024) %>%
  mutate(
    # Use case_when() because cut() does not translate to SQL
    age_bucket = case_when(
      AGE >= 16 & AGE <= 24 ~ "16-24",
      AGE >= 25 & AGE <= 34 ~ "25-34",
      AGE >= 35 & AGE <= 44 ~ "35-44",
      AGE >= 45 & AGE <= 54 ~ "45-54",
      AGE >= 55 & AGE <= 64 ~ "55-64",
      AGE >= 65 ~ "65+"
    ),
    
    # Identify groups
    group = ifelse(HISPAN == 2 | HISPAND == 200 | ANCESTR1 == 261, "Puerto Rican", "All Others"),
    
    # Create a weighted labor force variable for easy SQL summing
    # If in labor force (2), use their weight. If not (1), assign 0.
    weighted_lf = ifelse(LABFORCE == 2, PERWT, 0)
  ) %>%
  
  # Group and summarize on the server to dramatically shrink the data size
  group_by(YEAR, group, age_bucket) %>%
  summarise(
    pop_in_bucket = sum(PERWT, na.rm = TRUE),
    lf_in_bucket = sum(weighted_lf, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = 'drop'
  ) %>%
  
  # EXECUTE THE QUERY: Pull this small, summarized dataframe into local R memory
  collect()
```


```{r Age adjusted wrangling, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# 3. Local-Side Analysis (Age Adjustment)
# Now that we have the summarized data locally, we can run the math instantly

# A. Calculate standard population weights (Pooled 2001-2024 US Population)
standard_pop <- server_aggregated_data %>%
  group_by(age_bucket) %>%
  summarise(total_people = sum(pop_in_bucket)) %>%
  mutate(std_weight = total_people / sum(total_people)) %>%
  select(age_bucket, std_weight)

# B. Calculate Age-Specific Rates for each group/year
age_specific_rates <- server_aggregated_data %>%
  mutate(age_specific_lfpr = lf_in_bucket / pop_in_bucket)

# C. Merge weights and calculate the final Crude and Adjusted rates
final_results <- age_specific_rates %>%
  left_join(standard_pop, by = "age_bucket") %>%
  group_by(YEAR, group) %>%
  summarise(
    # Crude Rate: (Total in LF) / (Total Pop)
    crude_lfpr = sum(lf_in_bucket) / sum(pop_in_bucket),
    
    # Age-Adjusted Rate: Sum of (Age-Specific Rate * Standard Weight)
    adjusted_lfpr = sum(age_specific_lfpr * std_weight),
    
    total_pop_16plus = sum(pop_in_bucket),
    .groups = 'drop'
  ) %>%
  # Format percentages
  mutate(
    crude_lfpr = round(crude_lfpr * 100, 2),
    adjusted_lfpr = round(adjusted_lfpr * 100, 2)
  ) %>%
  arrange(YEAR, group)

print(final_results)
```

```{r Age adjusted analysis, message=FALSE,warning=FALSE}
# 4. Create the final comparison table
comparison_table <- final_results %>%
  select(YEAR, group, adjusted_lfpr) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = group, values_from = adjusted_lfpr) %>%
  mutate(gap = `Puerto Rican` - `All Others`)

print(comparison_table)
```
